name: Buffy Olive
lede: Buffy Olive is a muted grayish-olive brown, and one of the most common names in our painting archive, found in nearly one painting in five.

sections.title: Buff meets olive
sections.body: Our library dates Buffy Olive to Ridgway's 1912 standards, plate XXX, hue 21′′, with the 1955 ISCC-NBS system classing a close match as a light olive [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[citrine-drab]], [[gold-fusion]], [[baiko-brown]] and [[hair-brown]], at 2.6, 2.8, 6, 2.8, 3.2 and 3.2 ΔE [1]. A fifth, slightly farther neighbor is [[rustic-drab]], 3.4 ΔE away, more vivid [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a close match to Buffy Olive in 4,476 of 23,781 paintings, 18.82 percent, as photographed[2]. It most often plays a light tone inside a painting (39 percent of appearances), rather than a shadow or accent [2].

Kristian Zahrtmann used it most relative to his own museums' baseline, in 7 of his 18 works here, 3.4 times expected [2]. It keeps company with Brownish Olive and Sand far more than chance, and the earliest dated match, from 916, is almost a thousand years before the 1912 record, a floor set by the archive's thin early coverage rather than a claim about the color's age [2].
